author: product-requirements-expert
title: Veterinarian directory narrowed by specialty
summary: The veterinarian directory, in both its page form and its machine-readable form, accepts an optional specialty name and lists only the veterinarians holding it. Naming nothing leaves both surfaces exactly as they are today.
acceptance_criteria: Both /vets.html and /vets accept an optional specialty query parameter; the value is a specialty name.
A named specialty held by some veterinarians narrows the listing to exactly those veterinarians, on both surfaces.
Matching is on the whole specialty name and ignores letter case; a value that is only part of a stored specialty name matches nothing.
A specialty no veterinarian holds, and a value that is no specialty at all, both answer HTTP 200 with an empty veterinarian list on both surfaces.
A specialty value that is empty or entirely whitespace behaves as if the parameter were absent, mirroring empty owner search under REQ-OWN-002.
An absent specialty parameter preserves today's behavior exactly on both surfaces: the page stays paged as before, and the machine-readable list stays unpaged and complete.
Pagination links on the narrowed page carry the specialty value, so moving between pages keeps the narrowing.
Page numbering and the reported total reflect the narrowed set, not the whole directory.
The narrowed page renders through the existing directory template with no new page control.
Tests cover each criterion above, including the empty-value, no-match, case-insensitive, partial-name, and pagination-link cases, on both surfaces.
non_goals: Any visible page control for the filter - no form, dropdown, link list, or chip. The narrowing travels in the URL only. A visible control is a candidate follow-up request and is recorded as an open question in docs/prd.md.

Free-text or prefix search over veterinarians, pets, or visits. NG-9 is narrowed to admit attribute filtering of the veterinarian directory only - see docs/adr/2026-08-08-non-goal-veterinarian-search.md.
Narrowing by more than one specialty in one request.
Narrowing by any attribute other than specialty.
Adding paging to the machine-readable list, or any other change to it beyond accepting the specialty parameter.
Managing veterinarians or specialties through the application - NG-2 stands.
A no-match message on the narrowed page. Owner search reports 'no owner found'; this slice lists nothing silently. Recorded as an open question.
notes: Fresh REQ minted; REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and is not a predecessor. Three PRD reconciliations landed with this entry: the Veterinarian directory known-defect edge case for the second route is removed, the Superseded entry for REQ-VET-002 no longer says 'pending removal', and the answered open question about REQ-VET-002 carries a 2026-08-08 revisit note. NG-9 narrowed in the Non-Goals table and preamble. Two follow-ups fall outside this agent's write scope and belong to system-design-expert: docs/system-design.md line 207 carries a Known Defects row saying the machine-readable vet route 'serves no requirement' and 'remains pending removal' - that row is now false and should be dropped; and docs/adr/README.md needs an index row for docs/adr/2026-08-08-non-goal-veterinarian-search.md. Added 'Veterinarian directory' to docs/ubiquitous-language.md. Note the two surfaces differ today: /vets.html is paged, /vets is not - the filter applies to both, paging behavior is unchanged on each.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The narrowing reuses the paged attribute-search shape the owner feature already teaches: a normalized request parameter delegated to a derived Spring Data query, with no service layer (ADR 2026-07-31-feature-package-organization). Two things are new ground and are now recorded in durable memory. First, the specialty lookups must stay out of the vets cache, because that cache has no size limit and no eviction and the key would be caller-supplied text - ADR 2026-08-08-uncached-specialty-filtered-vet-lookup, plus a new Threat Model row in system-design.md. Second, the machine-readable route is now a supported surface: its Known Defects row is removed, and the Vets, VetRepository, and VetController contract rows are re-pointed at REQ-VET-003.
integration_points: VetRepository gains two specialty lookups - a paged one for /vets.html and an unpaged one for /vets. VetRepository extends Repository rather than JpaRepository, so both arities must be declared explicitly; nothing is inherited.

Neither new repository method carries @Cacheable. findAll() and findAll(Pageable) keep their existing @Cacheable("vets") annotations unchanged, so the unnarrowed directory keeps today's cache behavior.

VetController normalizes the specialty once in a private helper shared by both handlers. The acceptance criteria demand identical matching, blank, and no-match semantics on both surfaces, and one shared normalization is what keeps them from drifting.
The paging asymmetry is preserved deliberately: /vets.html stays paged with its existing page size, /vets stays unpaged and complete. The filter composes with each surface as it stands.
vetList.html model gains the normalized specialty value (null when absent) so the pagination block can carry it.

patterns.description: Paged attribute search: strip the request parameter, then delegate to a derived repository query and feed the Page into the pagination model. Follow this shape, but note one deliberate divergence - owner search maps a blank value to an empty prefix that matches everything, whereas a blank specialty must branch to the unfiltered query, since a whole-name match on an empty string matches nothing. Copying owner's blank handling verbatim breaks the blank-value criterion.

Derived query returning Page, no @Query text. For this slice use the Distinct + IgnoreCase form over the association property - findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String, Pageable) and the unpaged sibling. Plain Name (not StartingWith or Containing) delivers whole-name matching, so a partial name matches nothing; IgnoreCase normalizes case inside the query rather than relying on the vendor collation; Distinct guards against a vet joining more than once.

The existing pagination block builds hrefs with Thymeleaf preprocessing (@{'/vets.html?page=__${i}__'}). Convert these to the link-parameter form @{/vets.html(page=${i}, specialty=${specialty})}. Two properties come free: the caller-supplied value is URL-encoded on the way into the href, and a null specialty is omitted entirely, which leaves today's link shape byte-identical when no specialty is named.

risks.risk: Annotating the new repository methods @Cacheable("vets") for symmetry with their neighbours would key a cache that has no size limit and no eviction on arbitrary caller text, letting any client grow it without bound.
risks.mitigation: ADR 2026-08-08-uncached-specialty-filtered-vet-lookup records the decision and the rejected alternatives; the new methods carry no cache annotation, and a Threat Model row in system-design.md makes the exclusion visible to the security reviewer.

risks.risk: Leaning on the database collation for case-insensitive matching would repeat the PostgreSQL owner-search defect, where the same query returns different results per vendor.
risks.mitigation: The IgnoreCase derived keyword normalizes both sides inside the generated JPQL, so the match is identical on H2, MySQL, and PostgreSQL. The H2-backed suite cannot observe a collation divergence, which is exactly why the normalization belongs in the query.

risks.risk: Building the pagination hrefs by string concatenation would place caller-supplied text into the page unencoded.
risks.mitigation: Thymeleaf's link-parameter syntax URL-encodes the value; default output escaping stays on. Both are required by security-principles.md's cross-site-scripting row.

risks.risk: Paging a query that joins the EAGER ManyToMany association can make Hibernate paginate in memory rather than in SQL.
risks.mitigation: The pagination-link test must cross a page boundary on a narrowed set, and the implementer should check the build log for a collection-fetch pagination warning. Consult if it appears - the fallback is an explicit @Query with a fetch-free join.

risks.risk: An unknown or non-existent specialty could be treated as an error rather than an empty result.
risks.mitigation: The PRD closes this: HTTP 200 with an empty list on both surfaces. The filter only ever narrows, never widens, so the failure direction is closed rather than open. No allowlist validation of the value is wanted.

notes: Both doc reconciliations named in the prd-entry are applied. (1) The Known Defects row claiming the machine-readable route serves no requirement is removed, and the document provenance line is corrected from four confirmed defects to three. Open Question 5 now reads 'unfiltered read methods are cached'. (2) docs/adr/README.md gains index rows for the non-goal veterinarian-search ADR and for the new cache ADR. Additionally the Vets contract row moves from an Implements of em-dash to REQ-VET-003, which also repairs a standing inconsistency - the paragraph above that table lists only three kinds of em-dash contract and Vets was an unlisted fourth. Security notes for the reviewer: VetController binds only @RequestParam scalars and no command object, so the mass-assignment disallow-list row is not engaged and no @InitBinder is wanted here. No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so the autofix audit is empty.

author: change-grader
summary: narrow the veterinarian directory by specialty

blast_radius.note: Code reach is confined to the vet package and its one template: two derived repository lookups, one controller parameter with a shared normalizer, and the five pagination links in vetList.html. No sensitive paths, no build, schema, config, or cache-configuration edits, and both routes stay backward compatible with the parameter absent. The 40 hunks are inflated by six documentation files and by rewriting each pagination link individually.

semantic_surprise.note: The one hunk that could hide a silent behavior change is the pagination rewrite from literal substitution (@{'/vets.html?page=__${i}__'}) to parameterized link expressions, and it is pinned: the unnarrowed branch renders the original shape and a test asserts the string /vets.html?page=2 with no 'specialty' substring. normalizeSpecialty collapses null, empty, and whitespace to null, which selects the unfiltered listing rather than a query that would match nothing, and both surfaces share it so they cannot drift. Distinct paging over the specialties join reports totals for the narrowed set, proven against the real database rather than asserted against a stub.

test_adequacy.note: The split is real, not tautological: matching semantics (whole name, case-insensitive, partial matches nothing, narrowed paging totals) are pinned in ClinicServiceTests against H2 with real seed data, while VetControllerTests drives the MVC stack for wiring, model attributes, and rendered link markup.
